subjects.term: MSC2020 82B20: Lattice systems (Ising, dimer, Potts, etc.) and systems on graphs arising in equilibrium statistical mechanics

title: Every Site Hears the Same: the Loop Equality Is a Theorem
description:
Theorem 1 (the Loop Equality, the conjecture of #74). On the tetrahedral network of every close-packed stacking (diamond 3C, lonsdaleite 2H, the polytypes 4H, 6H, 9R and every other stacking, periodic or not), at every site, the number of closed non-backtracking loops of each length m equals the number for diamond: 24, 48, 480, 3432, 25704, ... for m = 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, ..., given by the Ihara–Bass formula from the Domb numbers. In Fourier space over the layers the stacking only decides whether a step across a bond layer uses a triangle of bond directions or its point mirror, and a closed walk crosses every bond layer as often upwards as downwards, so the choice cancels; non-backtracking loops are reduced to ordinary walks between the two ends of a bond. Corollaries: the same holds on the pyrochlore network of every stacking (spin ice) and on the sphere packing of every close-packed stacking. The closed-walk part was known (Nagle 1966 for ice; Thorpe 1972 for all periodic polytypes), and for periodic stackings the site-averaged loop counts also follow from Thorpe's result and the Bass formula for periodic graphs (Guido, Isola and Lapidus 2008); new are the loop statement at every single site, aperiodic stackings and the two corollaries. Exact integer counts on 42 stackings, including 30 random ones, Fibonacci approximants and the aperiodic Fibonacci stacking, agree at all 686 sites tested.

The Loop Equality surfaced, unexpected by DICTO or Claude, in the loop counts computed for DICTO's study of stackings (#74), which stated it as a conjecture for all lengths. Proof, checks and drafting with Claude (Anthropic).

Version 3 corrects the account of the origin (the equality surfaced, unexpected, in the loop counts computed for DICTO's study #74; it was not foreseen) and the link to the data, which now points to a fixed commit. No result changes.

Version 4 follows the check of the paper on aiXiv (2611.01038): it states the 60° angle that facts (i)–(ii) use, writes out the proof of Corollary 3 for the two kinds of touching spheres, credits the site-averaged loop counts for periodic stackings to Thorpe with Guido, Isola and Lapidus, and describes the literature searched instead of listing private catalogue files. No result changes.
